abstract: The CIViC (Clinical Interpretations of Variants in Cancer) knowledgebase (https://civicdb.org) remains one of the few free, unrestricted knowledgebases for the distribution of somatic cancer variant interpretations. CIViC leverages public curation and expert moderation to address the bottleneck problem of cancer variant interpretation for patient care. As the curation platform for ClinGen Somatic Cancer, the CIViC knowledge model is informed by multiple experts across disparate fields in cancer and, in turn, acts as a model for cancer variant classification and representation. In order to capture a wider range of genomic variations, several updates to CIViC's data and curation model have been made with a focus on maintaining familiar workflows and user interface layouts. A new top-level entity called the Feature represents Genes, Fusions, Regions for large-scale structural variations, and Factors for genome-wide biomarkers. Accompanying Variants capture information unique to each genomic event. Molecular Profiles enable the curation of complex combinations of these Variants. CIViC has also developed a system for approval and submission of Assertions to ClinVar, guidance for the use of AI in curation and moderation of content, and additional capabilities such as source retraction monitoring and an advanced query builder.
